result.rationale: The diff contains `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...));` — combining the two role checks with `&&` instead of `||`. A user is unlikely to hold both roles, so this almost always evaluates false, denying team admins/owners who aren't the organizer or an attendee, contradicting the variable's name and evident intent. The mechanism is fully visible in the diff and is a real authorization defect introduced by this change.

judged_text: The authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so isTeamAdminOrOwner is always false for any user (a membership has exactly one role, so no user is both admin and owner), making the team-admin path dead code. Team admins/owners who are not the booking organizer or an attendee receive FORBIDDEN ('you_do_not_have_permission') when trying to add guests to their own team's bookings, even though the code clearly intends to permit them; only the organizer and existing attendees can use the feature on team events.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning the check only passes if the user is *both* a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and intended permission path, this likely should be an OR; as written, a user who is only an admin or only an owner will fail the permission gate and may hit the `FORBIDDEN` branch unless they are also the organizer or an existing attendee.
